items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: You were telling me that during your long friendship with Strayhorn you repeatedly asked him for just eight bars?

ctx.x: A lot of things about Duke had changed. The band had changed considerably. And I think that his thinking about the band, the very thing, the kind of things the band was playing, along those times -- along about that time, were -- well, some of them, so far as I'm concerned, didn't make it. I felt cheated. Now, this could have been by the fact that, you know, maybe Johnny's gone and Strayhorn was gone, and the trumpet section was kind of in an uproar back there. And Duke was more or less getting in his ivory…
who's going to fault that? Everybody gets old.
